title: Women’s freeski halfpipe, Eileen Gu’s final Olympic event, postponed due to snow
content:
CORTINA D’AMPEZZO, Italy — Snowy weather in Livigno has impacted the Olympics again, postponing the women’s freestyle skiing halfpipe final originally scheduled for Saturday night.

The last event in the town that has hosted snowboarding and freestyle skiing, it was set to begin at 7:30 p.m. local (1:30 p.m. ET), but persistent snowfall in the area forced a postponement. It’s now scheduled for 10:40 a.m. local (4:40 a.m. ET) Sunday morning, the final day of the 2026 Games.

Eileen Gu, the 22-year-old star who competes for China and is the defending gold medalist in the event, qualified fifth for the final. Great Britain’s Zoe Atkin is the top qualifier.

Snow also impacted several events in the region earlier this week, causing postponements.

Last week, Gu criticized the scheduling of the freestyle events. Progressing to the big air final forced her to miss one of the three available training sessions for her preferred halfpipe event. She also competed in slopestyle in the opening days of the Games, winning silver in that and big air.

“At this point, I’m exhausted,” she said after halfpipe qualifying Thursday. “And the thing is, no judge is giving me extra points for being good at rails. No judge is giving me extra points because I missed a training. I’m the only one in this field competing in one other event, let alone two, but I still have to compete against the best of this event.”
